# ui::testing::HeadlessTextMeasurer

Header: `winui/testing/HeadlessUI.hpp`.

Derives from `ui::TextMeasurer`.

Deterministic, platform-independent text metrics. They don't match the real text renderer's metrics, but they make layout reproducible in tests and on any OS.

Every code point advances by [`font_size * AdvanceRatio`](#advanceratio) (nudged by weight, plus character spacing); a line is [`font_size * LineRatio`](#lineratio) tall unless the style sets a line height. The semantic goldens are laid out with it. [HeadlessUI](headless-ui.md) owns one; construct your own to measure or lay out a bare element in a test.

Example: 
```cpp
const ui::testing::HeadlessTextMeasurer measurer;
ui::TextStyle style;
style.font_size = 20.0f;
const ui::Size one = measurer.measure("abcd", style);
REQUIRE(one.width == 4 * 20.0f * ui::testing::HeadlessTextMeasurer::AdvanceRatio);

ui::ButtonControl button{"OK"};
const ui::Size desired = button.measure(ui::Size{200, ui::Unbounded}, measurer, ui::Theme::default_light());
```

## AdvanceRatio

```cpp
static float AdvanceRatio = 0.55f
```

The advance width per em, a rough monospace stand-in for a proportional UI font.

## LineRatio

```cpp
static float LineRatio = 1.35f
```

[Line](../controls/shapes.md#uiline) height per em, used when [TextStyle::line_height](../rendering/text-style.md#line_height) is unset.

## BaselineRatio

```cpp
static float BaselineRatio = 0.8f
```

The baseline's depth into a line, as a share of the line height.

## weight_advance_factor

```cpp
static float weight_advance_factor(FontWeight w)
```

A weight-dependent nudge on top of AdvanceRatio. Lighter weights sit slightly narrower and heavier ones slightly wider, so a semantic golden orders weights correctly.

## measure

```cpp
TextMetrics measure(std::string_view text, const TextStyle& style) const override
```

One line of `text`: code points times the advance, by one line height. `\n` is not treated as a break here; [measure_wrapped()](#measure_wrapped) handles it.

## measure_wrapped

```cpp
TextMetrics measure_wrapped(std::string_view text, const TextStyle& style, float max_width) const override
```

The run broken into lines no wider than `max_width` per `style.wrapping`: the widest line's width and the height of all lines together. A width of 0 or less, an infinite one ([ui::Unbounded](../core/namespace-ui.md#unbounded)), or a NoWrap style, is [measure()](#measure). The default ignores wrapping altogether; both shipped measurers override it.
